answer: One garden plot per identity, bounded by onyx stones, locks an 80-credit bond. Each epoch it files copper readings, garden moisture, and onyx serials. An auditor recomputes copper resistance from a moisture table and checks onyx serials. Over 3% off, a reused serial, or two identities on one plot burns the bond. Filing k under one key costs 37+7(k-1); the 1,000th costs 7,030, so 1,000 fakes pay 3,533,500 plus 80,000 bonds. A rented-garden ring fails: rented probes carry the owner's key and mismatch the tenant filing, so both burn. An honest gardener pays 37 once and recovers it after audit.
